text.p: Following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The ruling coalition may break up as the government holds its emergency session today, attempting to resolve the differences between the Coalition and Reform parties.
- The Reform Party and Fatherland Union fell out in Tartu and coalition negotiations in the city council have been suspended.
- Numerous former state-owned enterprises have been taken over by shady firms which have proven incapable of running them.
- The parliament amended the law on sales tax, enabling leasing firms to deduct sales tax. The previous law caused major losses to the firms.
- The Fatherland Union intends to submit an alternative budget, which will reduce taxes and allocate more funds to education, emergency services and road maintance.
- The sale of a plot of land in Viimsi near Tallinn to President Lennart Meri may be canceled as the area may contain the historic remains of a chapel and cemetery.
- The government will sell the shares of hotel Olympia but will retain ownership of the high-rise building.
